system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: model serving APIs
G2: Kubernetes
G3: MLflow
G4: Airflow/Kubeflow
G5: deep learning beyond a course
G6: GCP infrastructure
G7: CI/CD for ML

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Claiming he deployed models as APIs or built ML pipelines on Kubernetes/Kubeflow
T2: Listing MLflow, Airflow, Kubernetes, SageMaker because MLE ads require them
T3: Presenting the PyTorch course project as professional deep learning
T4: Claiming he deployed the Streamlit app to Cloud Run (platform team did)
T5: Retitling him as ML Engineer in the experience section
T6: Old cover letter is to his current employer and describes him as junior analyst

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Data Scientist with experience developing and evaluating forecasting and churn models, customer
segmentation, and experimentation tools. Uses Python, SQL and R to build analytical solutions for
operational and product decisions. Experience includes scheduled notebook workflows, batch scoring,
feature engineering, and automated tests.
EXPERIENCE
Data Scientist | Thistlebox | 2022-Present
• Developed a six-week weekly demand forecast by recipe and region using LightGBM with calendar,
price and menu-position features. The scheduled notebook writes forecasts to BigQuery for
operations reporting in Looker; WAPE improved from 23% to 14%, with an estimated 9%
reduction in food waste.
• Built an XGBoost churn propensity model scored weekly in BigQuery, with retention offers sent to
top-decile customers. A 10% holdout validation found churn was 2.1 percentage points lower in the
treated group.
• Developed a Streamlit sequential A/B testing calculator for planning and analysing experiments;
used by approximately 25 people in product and growth. Wrote the app and its Dockerfile; the
data platform team handles deployment to Cloud Run.
• Since 2025, writing pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code; coverage is approximately 60%.
• Delivered the internal training “Stats for PMs” three times.
Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail | 2020-2022
• Segmented customers and analysed tariffs using R and SQL.
• Automated monthly regulator reports with R Markdown, saving the team approximately two days
each month.
PROJECT
Image Classification Course Project | Personal | 2025
• Fine-tuned a small CNN on a public food images dataset as part of an online deep learning course;
achieved approximately 80% accuracy. Learning project.
EDUCATION
MSc in Statistics
• Dissertation on Bayesian hierarchical models.
SKILLS
Programming and analysis: Python, pandas, scikit-learn, SQL, R, R Markdown
Machine learning and statistics: LightGBM, XGBoost, SHAP, statsmodels, feature engineering,
forecasting, churn modelling, experimentation, Bayesian hierarchical models
Data and deployment tools: BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, dbt, Looker, Streamlit, Docker
Testing and deep learning: pytest, PyTorch, torchvision (course project)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. In my current
Data Scientist role at Thistlebox, I have developed and evaluated forecasting and churn
models, and built an experimentation tool used by product and growth colleagues. This work
has given me a practical foundation in developing useful ML solutions with operational and
product teams.
My work includes a weekly churn model scored in BigQuery and a scheduled six-week demand
forecast that writes results to BigQuery for operations to use in Looker. The forecast
improved WAPE from 23% to 14%, with an estimated 9% reduction in food waste. I also built
a Streamlit sequential testing calculator used by approximately 25 colleagues, wrote its
Dockerfile, and have been adding pytest unit tests to forecasting feature code since 2025.
I am now looking to grow from data science into production-focused machine learning
engineering. Quillstone’s focus on helping merchants get support quickly, and the AI team’s
work alongside backend engineers, data scientists and product managers, make this role
particularly compelling to me. I would value the opportunity to bring my modeling,
experimentation and Python experience to that work while developing further on the
production engineering side.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how
my experience could contribute to Quillstone’s Customer Operations AI team.
Kind regards,
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
